process_steps.input_state: as-received powder in stainless steel capsule

evidence.quote: The vessel underwent degassing at 200 °C to remove vapor and contaminants from the powder. After degassing, crimping and welding of one end of the stem were carried out until the vacuum level in the capsule reached 10−2 Torr.
The samples were then heated to 880, 930 and 980 °C, and pressurized up to 1000 bar, at a heating rate of 5 °C min−1 in phase.
Following HIP, the containers were removed and the specimens were machined via an electron beam discharge process.

fine equiaxed microstructures (HT-1) exhibited higher yield and tensile stresses than coarse equiaxed structures (HT-2) or lamellar phase morphology (HT-3), demonstrating the hardening effect resulting from grain size refinement.
Microstructures with finer equiaxed morphologies exhibited a slightly lower strain than those of coarser ones; this result was attributed to the nucleation and growth of voids during deformation.
